summary: Stacked usage charts now stack per-vCPU/per-core CPU raw, each at 0-100%, on an axis of 100% per visible vCPU, so four fully busy vCPUs fill a 400% chart instead of being scaled down to a 0-100% total. API impact: none; a presentation change over the existing stats history response.

guide.reason: The Stacked step now says each vCPU or core keeps its own 0-100% and the axis runs to 100% per vCPU.

api.reason: API impact: none. Only the browser's stacking arithmetic and axis range changed; the stats history endpoint, its series shape and the Core sampler are untouched.

roadmap.reason: Presentation fix within the delivered usage-history feature; no roadmap page changes.

state.reason: The Stacked toggle is per-page UI state and history stays host-reported; nothing is stored.

verification.method: Ran: node web/src/stats.test.mjs (passes: raw stacking [4,10]/[10,30], 200% axis for two vCPUs, 100% with one hidden), npm --prefix web run typecheck and build (clean), python3 tests/integration/managed_vm_browser.py --simulated with the phase1 QA venv (exit 0; 'Stacked CPU chart with vCPU 1 hidden' passed with 83 single-fill pixels before and after, 0 overlapping; the inspected capture shows vCPU 0 and vCPU 2 at 60% each stacking to 120% on a 200% axis), python3 scripts/check_docs.py --worktree (passed) and the repository privacy unit test (OK). Simulated agent only; ignored local capture not linked from this public record.
